distinguishing_features: Uses pneumatic flow-rate and pressure as gating signals for a tension release mechanism
Dynamically releases cable tension only at maximum joint extension to reduce stress amplitude
Couples the tensioning system directly to the actuator's pneumatic supply lines for control
Implements a bypass mechanism based on TRIZ P5 (pre-setting the system state) to decouple tension during high-stress cycles
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Reducing cyclic fatigue stress amplitude in dress-pack cables at a robot wrist joint during high-stress motion phases without adding new sensors.
parsed.viable_reason: The mechanism is physically implausible as written because it assumes pneumatic supply line pressure and flow rate directly correlate with wrist joint position and cable tension, which is not a reliable or typical coupling in cobot design.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Even if viable, using pneumatic signals to gate a tensioning mechanism would be an obvious adaptation of prior art 3's approach of using existing signals for predictive control.
